korean-k1-l1.title: Basic vowels
korean-k1-l1.concept: Hangul na Korean alphabet. Every syllable dey inside a block. If vowel stand alone, write **ㅇ** before am, but e silent at di start: 아 na just “a”.

korean-k1-l2.title: Basic consonants
korean-k1-l2.concept: Put consonant before vowel to make syllable block: **ㄱ + ㅏ = 가** (ga). Read di block from left to right.

korean-k1-l3.title: First words
korean-k1-l3.concept: Join syllable blocks to form words. Read each block, then pronounce dem together.

korean-k1-l4.title: Y-vowels
korean-k1-l4.concept: Add short line to make **y** sound: ㅏ → ㅑ (ya), ㅓ → ㅕ (yeo), ㅗ → ㅛ (yo), ㅜ → ㅠ (yu). In modern Korean, ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e) sound very similar.
korean-k1-l4.example: 야 · 여 · 요 · 유 (ya · yeo · yo · yu)

korean-k1-l5.title: More consonants
korean-k1-l5.concept: ㄹ sound between “r” and “l”. ㅈ (j), ㅊ (ch with puff of air), ㅋ (k with puff of air), ㅌ (t with puff of air), and ㅍ (p with puff of air) complete basic consonants.
korean-k1-l5.example: 라 · 자 · 차 · 카 · 타 · 파 (ra · ja · cha · ka · ta · pa)

korean-k1-l6.title: Doubled consonants
korean-k1-l6.concept: ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ, and ㅉ be tense sounds. Say dem with tight throat and no puff of air, like first sound in “skate”.
korean-k1-l6.example: 까 · 따 · 빠 · 싸 · 짜 (kka · tta · ppa · ssa · jja)

korean-k1-l7.title: Final consonants
korean-k1-l7.concept: Consonant under syllable na **받침 (batchim)**. E close di syllable: 안 (an), 말 (mal), 밤 (bam), 강 (gang), 집 (jip), 책 (chaek). Only seven sounds fit come at di end: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ.
korean-k1-l7.example: 안 · 말 · 밤 · 강 · 집 (an · mal · bam · gang · jip)

korean-k1-l8.title: Everyday words
korean-k1-l8.concept: Read each word one syllable at a time. Dem pronounce 학교 as “hakgyo”: close di final ㄱ in 학 and pronounce di next syllable tightly.

korean-k1-l9.title: Words about the world
korean-k1-l9.concept: People and nature: 사람 (person), 나라 (country), 하늘 (sky), 산 (mountain), 강 (river), 꽃 (flower).

korean-k10-l1.title: Headlines and shortened style
korean-k10-l1.concept: News headlines and shortened noun phrases: 물가 안정 대책 발표.
korean-k10-l1.example: 물가 안정 대책을 발표했습니다. (mulga anjeong daechaegeul balpyohaesseumnida.) = announced plan to stabilize prices

korean-k10-l2.title: Current affairs and opinion articles
korean-k10-l2.concept: Read short news articles: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다.
korean-k10-l2.example: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다. (chinhwan-gyeong eneojiga jumokbatgo isseumnida.) = clean energy dey get attention

korean-k10-l3.title: Idioms about body parts (발, 눈, 귀, 손)
korean-k10-l3.concept: Common body-part idioms: 발이 넓다 (know plenty people), 눈이 높다 (get high standards).
korean-k10-l3.example: 김 대리는 발이 넓어요. (gim daerineun bari neobeoyo.) = know plenty people / 눈이 높아요. (nuni nopayo.) = choose according to high standards

korean-k10-l4.title: Everyday idioms (바가지, 어깨)
korean-k10-l4.concept: Expressions for everyday situations: 바가지를 쓰다 (get overcharged), 어깨가 무겁다 (have a heavy responsibility).
korean-k10-l4.example: 바가지를 썼어요. (bagajireul sseosseoyo.) = dem charge me too much / 어깨가 무거워요. (eokkaega mugeowoyo.) = get heavy responsibility

korean-k10-l5.title: Important Korean proverbs
korean-k10-l5.concept: Wisdom inside proverbs: 소 잃고 외양간 고친다, 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라.
korean-k10-l5.example: 소 잃고 외양간 고친다. (so ilko oeyanggan gochinda.) = repair di barn after losing cow / 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라. (soeppuldo dangime ppaera.) = do am while di iron hot

korean-k10-l6.title: Four-character idioms (사자성어)
korean-k10-l6.concept: Common four-character idioms from Chinese: 일석이조, 작심삼일, 다다익선.
korean-k10-l6.example: 일석이조예요. (ilseogijoyeyo.) = kill two birds with one stone / 작심삼일이에요. (jaksimsamirieyo.) = determination last only three days

korean-k10-l7.title: Logical connectors and discourse markers
korean-k10-l7.concept: Formal discourse markers: -에 따르면, 한편, 요컨대, 따라서.
korean-k10-l7.example: 의견에 따르면 그렇습니다. (uigyone ttareumyeon geureotsseumnida.) = according to di opinion / 한편 다른 측면도 있습니다. (hanpyeon dareun cheungmyeondo isseumnida.) = on di other hand, another aspect dey

korean-k10-l8.title: Deep Korean Cultural Values and Customs
korean-k10-l8.concept: Cultural ideas and holiday traditions: 따뜻한 정, 송편을 빚다.
korean-k10-l8.example: 따뜻한 정이 있어요. (ttatteutan jeongi isseoyo.) = warm affection / 송편을 빚어요. (songpyeoneul bijeoyo.) = make songpyeon for Chuseok

korean-k10-l9.title: Full K10 Review
korean-k10-l9.concept: Master Korean culture, media, idioms, and formal debate phrases.
korean-k10-l9.example: 일석이조의 효과를 거두었어요. (ilseogijoui hyogwareul geoduosseoyo.) = get two benefits at once / 상호 이해를 바탕으로 협력해요. (sangho ihaereul batangeuro hyeomnyeokaeyo.) = cooperate based on mutual understanding

korean-k2-l1.title: Hello and Thank You
korean-k2-l1.concept: Polite greetings end in **-요** or **-니다**. You fit use 안녕하세요 any time of di day.

korean-k2-l10.title: Signs You Will See
korean-k2-l10.concept: Short signs dey everywhere for Korea. **입구** mean entrance, **출구** mean exit, and **화장실** mean restroom. On doors, **미세요** mean push, and **당기세요** mean pull.

korean-k2-l11.title: Thank You for the Meal
korean-k2-l11.concept: Before meal, say **잘 먹겠습니다**; when you finish, say **잘 먹었습니다**. Host dey welcome you with **어서 오세요**, and **맛있어요** praise di food.
korean-k2-l11.example: 잘 먹겠습니다. (jal meokgetseumnida.) = Dem say am before eating: “I go enjoy di food.” / 잘 먹었습니다. (jal meogeotseumnida.) = Dem say am after eating: “I enjoy di food.”

korean-k2-l2.title: Yes, No, and Okay
korean-k2-l2.concept: Short polite answers wey you fit use every day. Korean add **요** at di end to sound polite.

korean-k2-l3.title: Nice to Meet You
korean-k2-l3.concept: When you meet new person, say 만나서 반갑습니다. There are two goodbye phrases: one for di person wey dey leave and one for di person wey dey stay.
korean-k2-l3.example: 만나서 반갑습니다. (mannaseo bangapseumnida.) = Nice to meet you.

korean-k2-l4.title: Polite Expressions
korean-k2-l4.concept: Use 실례합니다 to get person attention or pass by, 고마워요 to thank somebody in friendly way, 천만에요 to answer thank you, and 축하해요 to congratulate somebody.
korean-k2-l4.example: 실례합니다. (sillyehamnida.) = Excuse me. / 고마워요. (gomawoyo.) = Thank you. (friendly)

korean-k2-l5.title: Names and Countries
korean-k2-l5.concept: Ask for name with 이름이 뭐예요? and country with 어느 나라 사람이에요? Answer with 제 이름은 ___예요 or 저는 ___ 사람이에요.
korean-k2-l5.example: 이름이 뭐예요? (ireumi mwoyeyo?) = Wetin be your name?

korean-k2-l6.title: Saying Goodbye
korean-k2-l6.concept: Among friends, you fit say 잘 가요 (bye), 내일 봐요 (see you tomorrow), 또 만나요 (see you again), and 잘 자요 (sleep well).
korean-k2-l6.example: 잘 가요. (jal gayo.) = Bye. (friendly) / 내일 봐요. (naeil bwayo.) = See you tomorrow.

korean-k2-l7.title: How Are You?
korean-k2-l7.concept: Ask 잘 지냈어요? (You don dey okay?) and answer 잘 지내요 (I dey okay). 좋은 아침이에요 mean “Good morning.”
korean-k2-l7.example: 잘 지내요. (jal jinaeyo.) = I dey okay.

korean-k2-l8.title: Asking for Help
korean-k2-l8.concept: Say 도와주세요 to ask for help, 모르겠어요 when you no know, 알겠어요 when you understand, and 다시 말해 주세요 to ask somebody to repeat am.
korean-k2-l8.example: 도와주세요. (dowajuseyo.) = Abeg help me. / 알겠어요. (algesseoyo.) = I understand.

korean-k2-l9.title: Likes and Answers
korean-k2-l9.concept: 좋아요 mean good or fine; 싫어요 mean you no like am; 맞아요 mean “dat one correct”, and 틀려요 mean “dat one wrong”.
korean-k2-l9.example: 좋아요. (joayo.) = E good. / 싫어요. (sireoyo.) = I no like am.

korean-k3-l1.title: I Am a Student
korean-k3-l1.concept: **저는** mean “I” (polite). Add **이에요** after consonant, and **예요** after vowel, to say “I am ...”.
korean-k3-l1.example: 저는 학생이에요. (jeoneun haksaengieyo.) = I be student.

korean-k3-l10.title: Texting a Friend
korean-k3-l10.concept: Text messages use short polite sentences ending in **-요**. **지금 어디예요?** ask where you dey, **곧 가요** mean “I dey come soon”, and **늦어요** mean “I late”.
korean-k3-l10.example: 지금 어디예요? (jigeum eodiyeyo?) = Where you dey now? / 곧 가요. (got gayo.) = I dey come soon.

korean-k3-l11.title: Reading Words Aloud
korean-k3-l11.concept: When syllable end with consonant and next one start with vowel, di sound move over: 책이 dey pronounce **chaegi** and 밥을 dey pronounce **babeul**. Some sounds also change nearby sounds: 국물 dey pronounce **gungmul** and 같이 dey pronounce **gachi**.

korean-k3-l2.title: My Family
korean-k3-l2.concept: People use family words plenty in Korean, even for people wey no be their family.

korean-k3-l3.title: Counting
korean-k3-l3.concept: Korean get two number systems: native Korean (하나, 둘, 셋 …) to count things, and Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼 …) for money, dates, and minutes.

korean-k3-l4.title: Native Numbers 6–10
korean-k3-l4.concept: Continue native Korean numbers: 여섯 (6), 일곱 (7), 여덟 (8), 아홉 (9), 열 (10).
korean-k3-l4.example: 여섯 · 일곱 · 여덟 · 아홉 · 열 (yeoseot · ilgop · yeodeol · ahop · yeol)

korean-k3-l5.title: Sino-Korean Numbers
korean-k3-l5.concept: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 (1), 이 (2), 삼 (3), 사 (4), 오 (5), 육 (6), 칠 (7), 팔 (8), 구 (9), 십 (10). Dem dey use dem for money, dates, phone numbers, and minutes.
korean-k3-l5.example: 일 · 이 · 삼 · 사 · 오 · 육 · 칠 · 팔 · 구 · 십 (il · i · sam · sa · o · yuk · chil · pal · gu · sip)

korean-k3-l6.title: Age
korean-k3-l6.concept: Ask 몇 살이에요? (How old you be?). Ages use native numbers plus 살: 열 살 (10 years old), 스무 살 (20), 서른 살 (30).
korean-k3-l6.example: 몇 살이에요? (myeot sarieyo?) = How old you be?

korean-k3-l8.title: More Family Words
korean-k3-l8.concept: Siblings get different words depending on who dey speak: woman dey say 오빠 (older brother) and 언니 (older sister). Also learn 아들 (son), 딸 (daughter), 부모님 (parents).
korean-k3-l8.example: 오빠 (oppa) = older brother (woman dey say am) / 언니 (eonni) = older sister (woman dey say am)

korean-k3-l9.title: Our Family
korean-k3-l9.concept: Koreans often use 우리 (we, our) instead of “my”: 우리 가족 mean “my family”. Count people with 명: 네 명 (four people).

korean-k4-l1.title: Everyday Verbs
korean-k4-l1.concept: Polite present-tense verbs end with **-아요 / -어요 / -해요**. People use same form for “I”, “you”, and “they”.
korean-k4-l1.example: 먹어요. (meogeoyo.) = (I) dey chop. / 마셔요. (masyeoyo.) = (I) dey drink.

korean-k4-l2.title: Going to Places
korean-k4-l2.concept: Put **에** after a place to say where you dey go or come: 학교에 가요. Verb dey come last.
korean-k4-l2.example: 학교에 가요. (hakgyoe gayo.) = I dey go school.

korean-k4-l3.title: Eating, Drinking, Reading
korean-k4-l3.concept: The object of a verb takes **을** after consonant and **를** after vowel: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요.
korean-k4-l3.example: 밥을 먹어요. (babeul meogeoyo.) = I dey chop food.

korean-k4-l4.title: Food and Drinks
korean-k4-l4.concept: 밥 (rice, meal), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).

korean-k4-l5.title: Likes and Dislikes
korean-k4-l5.concept: Say wetin you like with -를/을 좋아해요 and wetin you no like with -를/을 싫어해요: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.

korean-k4-l6.title: Describing Things
korean-k4-l6.concept: Describing words also end with -요: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (plenty), 맛있어요 (delicious), 예뻐요 (fine).
korean-k4-l6.example: 커요. (keoyo.) = E big. / 작아요. (jagayo.) = E small.

korean-k4-l7.title: Weather
korean-k4-l7.concept: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (e hot), 추워요 (e cold), 비가 와요 (rain dey fall), 눈이 와요 (snow dey fall).
korean-k4-l7.example: 더워요. (deowoyo.) = E hot. / 추워요. (chuwoyo.) = E cold.

korean-k4-l8.title: Saying No with 안 and 못
korean-k4-l8.concept: Put **안** before verb to say you no dey do something (안 가요). Put **못** before am to say you no fit do am (못 가요).
korean-k4-l8.example: 안 먹어요. (an meogeoyo.) = I no dey chop.

korean-k4-l9.title: Daily Routine
korean-k4-l9.concept: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words like 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) use 에 after dem: 아침에.

korean-k5-l1.title: Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow
korean-k5-l1.concept: Time words usually dey near di start of sentence.

korean-k5-l2.title: Wetin I Did
korean-k5-l2.concept: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.

korean-k5-l3.title: Wetin I Go Do
korean-k5-l3.concept: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** for plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
korean-k5-l3.example: 내일 갈 거예요. (naeil gal geoyeyo.) = I go go tomorrow.

korean-k5-l4.title: Days of the Week
korean-k5-l4.concept: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).

korean-k5-l5.title: Months
korean-k5-l5.concept: Months na Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).

korean-k5-l6.title: Telling di time
korean-k5-l6.concept: Use native numbers with 시 to tell hour: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?
korean-k5-l6.example: 한 시 · 두 시 · 세 시 (han si · du si · se si)

korean-k5-l7.title: How often
korean-k5-l7.concept: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Put dem before verb.

korean-k5-l8.title: More past tense
korean-k5-l8.concept: Past ending na -았/었어요: 했어요 (did), 왔어요 (came), 만났어요 (met), 샀어요 (bought), 잤어요 (slept).

korean-k5-l9.title: Birthdays and weekends
korean-k5-l9.concept: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). Ask 생일이 언제예요? and answer 제 생일은 오월이에요.
korean-k5-l9.example: 생일이 언제예요? (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) = When your birthday be?

korean-k6-l1.title: For di shop
korean-k6-l1.concept: Ask di price with 얼마예요? Ask for something with **… 주세요** (… please).

korean-k6-l2.title: Where e dey?
korean-k6-l2.concept: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where e dey?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left), and 직진 (straight ahead).
korean-k6-l2.example: 화장실이 어디예요? (hwajangsiri eodiyeyo?) = Where toilet dey?

korean-k6-l3.title: I want to …
korean-k6-l3.concept: Add **-고 싶어요** to verb stem to say wetin you want do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.
korean-k6-l3.example: 가고 싶어요. (gago sipeoyo.) = I want to go.

korean-k6-l4.title: For restaurant
korean-k6-l4.concept: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I go order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, abeg), 계산해 주세요 (bring di bill, abeg).
korean-k6-l4.example: 계산해 주세요. (gyesanhae juseyo.) = Bring di bill, abeg.

korean-k6-l5.title: Moving around
korean-k6-l5.concept: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (subway), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Say how you dey travel with -로/으로: 버스로 가요.

korean-k6-l6.title: Phone calls and messages
korean-k6-l6.concept: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 mean “I call”.

korean-k6-l7.title: For hospital
korean-k6-l7.concept: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (e dey pain). Say body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head dey pain me).
korean-k6-l7.example: 병원 (byeongwon) = hospital / 아파요. (apayo.) = E dey pain.

korean-k6-l8.title: Polite Requests
korean-k6-l8.concept: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 make polite requests: 앉으세요 (abeg sit down), 기다려 주세요 (abeg wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (abeg open di door).

korean-k6-l9.title: Making Plans Together
korean-k6-l9.concept: 같이 (together) dey invite person: 같이 가요. 갈래요? mean “You want go?” and 시간 있어요? mean “You get time?”
korean-k6-l9.example: 같이 가요. (gachi gayo.) = Make we go together.

korean-k7-l1.title: Formal Polite Endings
korean-k7-l1.concept: For formal speech and work, add -ㅂ니다 to verb or adjective stem wey end with vowel, and -습니다 to stem wey end with consonant. Questions end with -ㅂ니까 / -습니까.
korean-k7-l1.example: 저는 학생입니다. (jeoneun haksaengimnida.) = I be student. / 이름이 무엇입니까? (ireumi mueosimnikka?) = Wetin be your name?

korean-k7-l10.title: Proportion and Inevitability (-을수록, -기 마련이다)
korean-k7-l10.concept: Learn “di more... di more” (-을수록) and things wey naturally dey happen (-기 마련이다).
korean-k7-l10.example: 만날수록 좋아요. (mannalsurok joayo.) = e dey better as we meet / 사람은 실수하기 마련이에요. (sarameun silsuhagi maryeonieyo.) = people sure dey make mistakes

korean-k7-l11.title: Appearance and Inference (-아/어 보이다, -는 모양이다)
korean-k7-l11.concept: Learn “look like” (-아/어 보이다) and “seem to be” (-는 모양이다).
korean-k7-l11.example: 행복해 보여요. (haengbokae boyeoyo.) = look happy / 비가 오는 모양이에요. (biga oneun moyangieyo.) = e look like say rain dey fall

korean-k7-l12.title: Pretending (-는 척하다)
korean-k7-l12.concept: Learn how to pretend to do or be something: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.
korean-k7-l12.example: 아는 척해요. (aneun cheokaeyo.) = e dey pretend to know

korean-k7-l13.title: Regret and Counterfactuals (-(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요)
korean-k7-l13.concept: Show regret: “I for don do...” -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요.
korean-k7-l13.example: 일찍 올 걸 그랬어요. (iljjik ol geol geuraesseoyo.) = I for don come early

korean-k7-l14.title: Full K7 Review
korean-k7-l14.concept: Review indirect speech, complex connectors, and subtle expressions.
korean-k7-l14.example: 친구가 온다고 했어요. (chinguga ondago haesseoyo.) = Friend say say e dey come / 같이 밥 먹자고 했어요. (gachi bap meokjago haesseoyo.) = suggest say make we chop together

korean-k7-l2.title: Plain forms
korean-k7-l2.concept: Plain written style end statements with -ㄴ다 / -는다, and past statements with -았다 / -었다. These forms be di base for reported speech in next lessons.
korean-k7-l2.example: 나는 학교에 간다. (naneun hakgyoe ganda.) = I dey go school. / 동생은 책을 읽는다. (dongsaengeun chaegeul ingneunda.) = My younger sibling dey read book.

korean-k7-l3.title: Describing nouns
korean-k7-l3.concept: Verb or adjective fit describe noun: use -(으)ㄴ for adjectives and past actions, -는 for present actions, -(으)ㄹ for future or planned actions. Put am before di noun.
korean-k7-l3.example: 저는 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요. (jeoneun masinneun eumsigeul joahaeyo.) = I like tasty food. / 예쁜 꽃을 샀어요. (yeppeun kkocheul sasseoyo.) = I buy fine flowers.

korean-k7-l4.title: Basic connectors
korean-k7-l4.concept: Connect two clauses with -아/어서 for reason or sequence, -지만 for contrast, -(으)니까 for reason, -(으)면 for condition, and -(으)려고 to show purpose.
korean-k7-l4.example: 피곤해서 일찍 잤어요. (pigonhaeseo iljjik jasseoyo.) = I tire, so I sleep early. / 비가 와서 집에 있었어요. (biga waseo jibe isseosseoyo.) = Rain fall, so I stay house.

korean-k7-l5.title: Ability, obligation, permission
korean-k7-l5.concept: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 show ability or possibility; -아/어야 하다 show obligation; -아/어도 되다 give permission.
korean-k7-l5.example: 저는 수영할 수 있어요. (jeoneun suyeonghal su isseoyo.) = I fit swim. / 저는 한국어로 이야기할 수 있어요. (jeoneun hangugeoro iyagihal su isseoyo.) = I fit talk Korean.

korean-k7-l6.title: Indirect statements (-다고 하다)
korean-k7-l6.concept: Report wetin somebody talk or don talk: verb or adjective + -다고 하다.
korean-k7-l6.example: 친구가 온다고 해요. (chinguga ondago haeyo.) = Friend talk say dem dey come.

korean-k7-l7.title: Indirect questions (-냐고 하다)
korean-k7-l7.concept: Report question with verb or adjective + -냐고 묻다/하다.
korean-k7-l7.example: 어디 가냐고 물었어요. (eodi ganyago mureosseoyo.) = Ask where person dey go.

korean-k7-l8.title: Indirect commands and suggestions (-라고 / -자고 하다)
korean-k7-l8.concept: Report a command (-라고 하다) or suggestion (-자고 하다).
korean-k7-l8.example: 빨리 오라고 했어요. (ppalli orago haesseoyo.) = Tell dem make dem come quickly / 같이 가자고 했어요. (gachi gajago haesseoyo.) = Suggest make we go together.

korean-k7-l9.title: Complex Causes and Contrasts (-느라고, -는데도)
korean-k7-l9.concept: Negative cause or delay (-느라고) and contrast even though something happen (-는데도).
korean-k7-l9.example: 공부하느라고 바빴어요. (gongbuhaneurago bapasseoyo.) = I dey busy because I dey study / 비가 오는데도 갔어요. (biga oneundedo gasseoyo.) = I go even though rain dey fall

korean-k8-l1.title: Honorific Words for Subjects
korean-k8-l1.concept: Special respectful nouns and verbs for people you respect: 진지, 주무시다, 편찮으시다.
korean-k8-l1.example: 할머니께서 진지를 드세요. (halmeonikkeseo jinjireul deuseyo.) = Grandma dey chop.

korean-k8-l2.title: Honorific Verbs for Objects (드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다)
korean-k8-l2.concept: Humble/respectful verbs when action dey directed to an elder: 드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다.
korean-k8-l2.example: 선물을 드려요. (seonmureul deuryeoyo.) = give gift respectfully / 내일 봬요. (naeil bwaeyo.) = see you tomorrow respectfully

korean-k8-l3.title: Passive Suffixes (-이/히/리/기-)
korean-k8-l3.concept: Make passive verbs by adding -이/히/리/기-: 보이다, 들리다, 열리다, 닫히다.
korean-k8-l3.example: 문이 열려요. (muni yeollyeoyo.) = door dey open / 창문이 닫혀요. (changmuni dachyeoyo.) = window dey close

korean-k8-l4.title: Passive Forms (-어지다, -게 되다)
korean-k8-l4.concept: Verbs wey take spontaneous or result passive forms: -아/어지다, -게 되다.
korean-k8-l4.example: 글씨가 써져요. (geulssiga sseojyeoyo.) = words dey write clearly / 알게 되었어요. (alge doeeosseoyo.) = I come to know

korean-k8-l5.title: Causative Suffixes (-이/히/리/기/우-)
korean-k8-l5.concept: Causative verbs wey make somebody do something: 보여 주다, 먹이다, 입히다.
korean-k8-l5.example: 사진을 보여 줘요. (sajineul boyeo jwoyo.) = show photo / 아기에게 밥을 먹여요. (agiege babeul meogyeoyo.) = feed baby

korean-k8-l6.title: Causative Form (-게 하다)
korean-k8-l6.concept: Make or cause somebody to do something: -게 하다.
korean-k8-l6.example: 웃게 해요. (utge haeyo.) = make somebody laugh / 기다리게 했어요. (gidarige haesseoyo.) = make somebody wait

korean-k8-l7.title: Public Formal Speech (-하십시오)
korean-k8-l7.concept: Very formal respectful style for announcements and ceremonies: -하십시오, -하십시다.
korean-k8-l7.example: 자리에 앉으십시오. (jarie anjeusipsio.) = Abeg sit down / 출발하십시다. (chulbalhasipsida.) = Make we comot

korean-k8-l8.title: Modest and Humble Expressions
korean-k8-l8.concept: Polite speech using humble pronouns and verbs: 저희, 말씀 올리다.
korean-k8-l8.example: 인사 말씀 올립니다. (insa malsseum ollimnida.) = I dey send my greetings / 저희 학교입니다. (jeohui hakgyoimnida.) = Na our school (humble form)

korean-k8-l9.title: K8 General Review
korean-k8-l9.concept: Review honorific speech, passive voice, causative forms, and formal polite language.
korean-k8-l9.example: 할머니께 선물을 드렸어요. (halmeonikke seonmureul deuryeosseoyo.) = I give gift to grandma / 문이 저절로 닫혔어요. (muni jeojeollo dachyeosseoyo.) = Di door close by itself

korean-k9-l1.title: Writing Business Emails and Making Requests
korean-k9-l1.concept: Formal business email expressions: -에 관하여, 검토 부탁드립니다.
korean-k9-l1.example: 회의 안건에 관하여 말씀드립니다. (hoeui angeone gwanhayeo malsseumdeurimnida.) = I dey write about di meeting agenda.

korean-k9-l2.title: Business Phone Etiquette
korean-k9-l2.concept: Handling calls and messages: 통화 가능하신지요, 연결해 드리겠습니다.
korean-k9-l2.example: 지금 통화 가능하신지요? (jigeum tonghwa ganeunghasinjiyo?) = You fit talk now? / 담당자를 연결해 드리겠습니다. (damdangjareul yeongyeolhae deurigetseumnida.) = I go connect you to di person in charge.

korean-k9-l3.title: Scheduling and Changing Appointments
korean-k9-l3.concept: Suggesting and changing appointment times: 변경하고자 합니다, 양해 부탁드립니다.
korean-k9-l3.example: 일정을 변경하고자 합니다. (iljeongeul byeongyeonghagoja hamnida.) = I wan change di schedule. / 너른 양해 부탁드립니다. (neoreun yanghae butakdeurimnida.) = Abeg bear with us.

korean-k9-l4.title: Meeting Discussions and Opinions
korean-k9-l4.concept: Sharing opinions during meetings: 제 생각으로는, 찬성합니다, 추가 검토.
korean-k9-l4.example: 제 생각으로는 이번 안이 좋습니다. (je saenggakeoroneun ibeon ani jotseumnida.) = For my mind, dis proposal good. / 적극 찬성합니다. (jeokgeuk chanseonghamnida.) = I agree well well.

korean-k9-l5.title: Reporting Project Progress
korean-k9-l5.concept: Giving updates: 진행 상황을 보고합니다, 조치를 완료했습니다.
korean-k9-l5.example: 프로젝트 진행 상황을 보고합니다. (peurojekteu jinhaeng sanghwangeul bogohamnida.) = I dey report project progress. / 조치를 완료했습니다. (jochireul wallyohaesseumnida.) = I don complete di action.

korean-k9-l6.title: Statistics and Data Trends
korean-k9-l6.concept: Describing trends and figures: 증가했습니다, 전년 대비.
korean-k9-l6.example: 매출이 증가했습니다. (maechuri jeunggahaesseumnida.) = Sales don increase. / 전년 대비 상승했습니다. (jeonnyeon daebi sangseunghaesseumnida.) = E don rise compared wit last year.

korean-k9-l7.title: Business Negotiations and Partnerships
korean-k9-l7.concept: Professional collaboration: 상호 협력을 희망합니다, 절충안 제시.
korean-k9-l7.example: 상호 협력을 희망합니다. (sangho hyeomnyeogeul huimanghamnida.) = We hope to work together. / 절충안을 제안합니다. (jeolchuganeul jeanhamnida.) = I dey suggest a compromise.

korean-k9-l8.title: Business Cards and Work Titles
korean-k9-l8.concept: Exchange of business cards and titles: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다.
korean-k9-l8.example: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다. (cheoeum boepgetseumnida, myeongham deurimnida.) = nice to meet you, here is my card / 김 부장님입니다. (gim bujangnimimnida.) = Department Manager Kim

korean-k9-l9.title: Full Review for K9
korean-k9-l9.concept: Review workplace communication, formal letters and meetings.
korean-k9-l9.example: 안건을 검토해 주시기 바랍니다. (angeoneul geomtohae jusigi baramnida.) = abeg review the agenda / 회의에서 뵙겠습니다. (hoeuieseo boepgetseumnida.) = see you for the meeting

texts.n:k.k3.sounds:linkC: Final consonant move join di next syllable if e start with silent consonant letter, so di sounds connect.
texts.n:k.k3.sounds:doubleC: For two final consonants, pronounce only one before another consonant. Before a vowel, di second one join di next syllable.
texts.n:k.k3.sounds:hDrop: H sound no pronounce after vowel or n, m, l, ng; then nearby sounds connect smoothly.
texts.n:k.k3.sounds:nasal: P, t, or k sound change to m, n, or ng when nasal consonant come after am.
texts.n:k.k3.sounds:rToN: L sound after stop consonant or ng pronounce as n, and stop consonant before am fit also change to nasal sound.

texts.n:k.k7.bridge_adnominal:adAdj: Adjective before noun take -(으)ㄴ after consonant or -ㄴ after vowel; words with 있다/없다 take -는.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_adnominal:adVerb: Verb before noun take -는 for present, -(으)ㄴ for past, and -(으)ㄹ for future or planned action.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_adnominal:adB: For ㅂ-irregular adjectives, ㅂ change to 우 before -ㄴ; ㄹ-verbs drop ㄹ before -는.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_adnominal:adn: Adnominal ending attach to verb or adjective before noun: past -(으)ㄴ, present -는 (or -ㄴ/은 for adjectives), future/planned -(으)ㄹ, and -던 for past habit or unfinished past action. Tense depend on when di described action happen, no be on main verb.

texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:cnSo: -아/어서 dey connect reason or order (do A, then B); no fit use am for requests, and tense show only for di final ending.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:cnBut: -지만 mean “but” and e join to normal stem of verbs, adjectives, and 이다.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:cnIf: -(으)면 mean “if/when”, while -(으)니까 give reason wey fit lead to request or discovery.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:cnPur: -(으)려고 + verb show purpose (“so as to”), and -는데/-(으)ㄴ데 set background or small contrast.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:cnAnd: -고 dey list actions or qualities in order (“and”).
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_connect:conn: Time connectors join to verb stem in fixed forms: -기 전에 (before), -(으)ㄴ 후에 (after), -(으)ㄹ 때 (when), -자마자 (as soon as). -(으)러 mean “so as to” only with 가다/오다 and similar movement verbs.

texts.n:k.k7.bridge_formal:fmForm: Formal polite statements end with -ㅂ니다 after a vowel and -습니다 after a consonant. For questions, use -ㅂ니까 / -습니까.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_formal:fmPast: Formal past tense na -았/었습니다, and formal future na -(으)ㄹ 겁니다. For questions, change 다 to 까.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_formal:fmL: If verb end with ㄹ, drop am before ㅂ, so formal form no get ㄹ before -ㅂ니다.
texts.n:k.k7.bridge_formal:formal: Use formal polite endings -ㅂ니다/-습니다 for statements and -ㅂ니까/-습니까 for questions at work, in announcements, and with customers. Add honorific -(으)시- only when respecting a person, no be for things or events.

texts.n:k.k7.bridge_modal:mdCan: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 mean “fit/can” (ability or possibility), and -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 mean “no fit/cannot”.

texts.g:ae29c713: Update on efforts to reduce permit processing time: This year average processing time na 41 days, 9 days shorter than last year. The main delay still dey happen during environmental impact consultation, wey account for 60 percent of all delayed cases. The responsible department go test a plan to handle consultation steps at the same time, but e no go shorten the legal review period. The time saved by doing things in parallel go come from reducing how often dem ask applicants to add missing documents. So the reduction in time go depend plenty on whether people submit complete documents from the beginning.
texts.g:d3bd3f83: Report on one forklift accident for the distribution center and the steps dem take after: During night work last month, forklift touch one worker for the loading area, but the worker only get small bruise. Instead, dem go finish separating the paths within two months and limit night work for that area until then.

texts.g:9454f6f5: One company check the number of people wey visit their online shop each month. The visitors increase steady from January reach March, but for the first time the number drop for April. The person in charge analyze say the reason na because complaints about late delivery don increase. So the company decide say dem go first find way to make delivery faster.
texts.g:f7c5d0c2: Report about the customer satisfaction survey. This year satisfaction score na 78, four points higher than last year's 74. But this year dem change how dem find people to answer, from phone call to online, and the share of online respondents wey dey in their 20s and 30s become double last year's own. Past surveys show say this age group too dey give scores wey pass average. So with the data wey dey now, e hard to know how much of the increase come from real improvement in service. We suggest say for the next survey dem compare using the same age-group shares as last year.
texts.g:e13c0f5b: Review comment on the results of the local small-business support programme. The average monthly sales of the 30 businesses wey get support increase by 18 percent compared with before the programme start. But when dem check each business, two of dem sales increase more than three times, while 21 actually drop small. If dem remove those two, the average increase rate go fall plenty. The department in charge conclude say the programme work overall, but with the figures wey dey above, evidence to support that conclusion no reach.
texts.g:700e4ddd: Report about road safety for the area. This year there were 1,200 road accidents, 6 percent more than last year, but the number of registered vehicles for the same period increase by 11 percent. When dem calculate accidents for every 10,000 vehicles, the rate actually reduce. But deaths remain at the same level as last year, so e hard to say the lower accident rate don lead to fewer serious accidents. The report recommend make dem interpret the number of accidents and how severe dem be as separate indicators.
texts.g:901fbaeb: According to one research institute report, over the last five years, cities and counties wey increase libraries show a trend of juvenile crime rate going down. But the report no conclude say na library expansion cause this, and e also mention say both things fit relate to the area's financial condition. This na because areas wey get enough money increase after-school programmes along with libraries. The institute add say to confirm the separate effect of library expansion, dem gats compare areas with similar financial conditions.
texts.g:3ca56d36: The results of the citizen opinion survey dey summarized here. For the project dem dey talk about, support na 62 percent, opposition 31 percent and no response 7 percent. But only 4 percent of the people respond, and people aged 65 or older make up 52 percent of respondents, far above their actual 24 percent share of the population. The research team also show figures adjusted to match the real age makeup of the population; after adjustment, support drop to 54 percent but still pass opposition. The team talk say support still dey ahead, but people suppose understand say the gap smaller than the original figures show.
texts.g:98ee0f8a: Report on third-quarter operating results. Net income na 12 billion won, about 35 percent higher than the same time last year. But 2.5 billion won of this na one-time profit from selling unused land. If dem remove that, net income growth stay in single digits. Also, operating profit, wey show the profit from the main business of selling products, drop by 2 percent. The finance team judge say e too early to read the increase in net income as sign say the business dey improve. Dem go review this assessment after dem check whether the same pattern repeat next quarter.
texts.g:67ee002c: Monthly report on housing market trend. This month, apartment sales for the capital region increase by 3 percent from last month, but if you look at the trend for the last three months, e don stay almost flat. The price index too increase only 0.2 percent, and that fit be a change within the margin of error. Meanwhile, people for the property business report say enquiries increase after loan interest rate drop, but transaction statistics never confirm this yet. So the report take the position say e too early to conclude the market don enter recovery.
texts.g:e7f9a5a1: One research institute survey 1,200 office workers: people wey work from home at least two times a week report average job satisfaction of 78 points, higher than the 65 points for people wey work from office. Based on this, the institute announce say remote work dey raise productivity. But the survey only ask people to rate their own satisfaction and no measure actual work results. Also, most people doing remote work dey in jobs where dem get plenty freedom, so e hard to tell whether the satisfaction gap come from the work arrangement or the kind of job. So these results alone no enough to conclude say remote work dey raise productivity.
texts.g:9d18f689: Across all households, housing costs take an average of 22 percent of income, the same level as five years ago. Some people use this to say the housing burden no change. But for the 20 percent of households with the lowest income, the share increase from 31 to 38 percent, while for the top 20 percent e drop from 15 to 12 percent. The increase for one group and the drop for the other cancel each other, so the average just remain the same. An average show the middle for everybody together, but e no show the changes between groups. So no be correct to jump from the same average to the conclusion say every household dey carry the same burden.
texts.g:36c84153: For first year after Hansol Library open, visitors increase by 40 percent compared with last year, and city conclude say reading culture spread among residents. But during same period, books borrowed increase only 3 percent. Most people for user survey say dem come to study inside reading room. Visitor count fit show how easy and comfortable facility be to use, but e no directly show how much people read. To claim say reading culture spread, dem need also show other measures, like number of books borrowed or time spent reading.
texts.g:877e9eb2: Officially, inflation this year na 2.1 percent, but plenty residents feel say living costs rise more than that. Because of dis gap, people criticize statistics say dem no reflect reality. But price index na number dem calculate by assigning weights to items according to average household spending. For a year when food prices rise 5 percent, low-income families wey spend plenty on food go feel higher rate than average. At di end, difference between official figure and wetin people feel no come from wrong calculations; e happen because one number no fit represent every household.
texts.g:70fd5ba4: Sales of new drink rise by 20 percent for three months after ads start in June, compared with previous three months. Marketing team show di graph as evidence say ads work. But demand for dis drink dey rise during summer, and even last year without ads, sales rise 18 percent for same time. If we consider dat, di increase caused by ads fit be only around 2 percentage points at most. Still, weather and other products fit be different last year, so even dis number hard to accept as confirmed effect.
texts.g:6a73ec88: When online shop run customer satisfaction survey, 35 percent of people answer “very dissatisfied”. Some executives think serious problem don happen with service. But only 12 percent of customers answer di survey, and customers with complaints more likely to answer. So we no fit treat 35 percent as opinion of all customers. But dis no mean say data useless. Reasons for dissatisfaction wey people write down fit give clues about which areas need improvement first.
texts.g:70ffd4cd: Average score of students wey skip breakfast 6 points lower pass students wey chop am. People often use dis result to claim say eating breakfast improve school grades. But when dem compare only students from families with similar income, di score gap reduce to 1.5 points. Na because students from low-income families more likely skip breakfast, and dem often get worse places to study too. Dis analysis no mean say breakfast no get any effect, but e clearly show say other things explain plenty of di gap wey dem see at first.

texts.g:afc76388: Today we go look at how to preserve hanok from point of view of cultural heritage policy. Hanok no be only house; e na cultural product wey carry climate and way of life inside. But if people change am for modern comfort, dem fit damage its special structure. So main issue na how to balance preserving and using am.
texts.g:5eec1ae4: A: People criticize local festivals say dem don become too business-like. B: Because dem use visitor numbers to judge success, local stories wey make each area special don become weaker in some ways. C: I see am different. Residents fit continue festival only if money dey come in, so e hard to oppose business activity itself. Important thing na to build system wey return di income to local community.
texts.g:83f2d8a3: Foundation dey announce results for its support program to preserve traditional crafts. Dis year dem choose 7 out of 30 applicant groups, and reviewers focus on whether skills fit pass to next generation and how strong group connection to local community be. texts.g:acba7a7b: A: People dey worry plenty say dialects dey disappear. Wetin you think cause am? B: Standard language spread widely through broadcasting and education, and young people moving to cities reduce chances to speak dialect. A: Wetin dem suppose do to preserve dialects? B: No just record dem; connect dem to local education so people fit really use dem every day.
texts.g:001b4b52: Topic of today lecture na how to handle cultural context in translation. Word-for-word translation get advantage because e stay close to original, but some meanings fit sound strange to readers. Free translation easier to read, but e fit remove character of original. We go compare strengths and weaknesses of both methods using examples.
texts.g:fedf0417: A: People dey argue plenty about the habit of asking somebody age first when dem meet. Wetin you think? B: Since Korean get different ways to address people and speak based on who the other person be, I see asking age as a practical way to set how the conversation go go. C: I understand that use, but no be say e make the older person end up leading the conversation as a fixed arrangement? B: I no deny say that side effect dey. But na something the custom cause, no be the reason the custom start. If the way people address each other change, people go naturally ask the question less too.
texts.g:fcb8250f: A: How we fit explain the culture of exchanging gifts during holidays and making sure to return one too? B: I see am as sign of trust wey last long. The wish to return wetin you receive become cord wey keep the relationship going. C: But if people try return exactly wetin dem receive, no be the same thing as transaction? B: For outside, e fit look like that. But if na transaction, the relationship go end as soon as payment complete. When person deliberately add small extra to the return gift so one debt remain, e mean say dem no intend to end the relationship. I no deny say calculation dey inside. Na just say the aim of that calculation na to continue, no be to settle account.
texts.g:46ef3493: A: Some people criticize everyday hanbok, the version dem adapt for daily wear, say e dey damage tradition. C: I think if dem no keep the structure, like the proportion between jacket and skirt and how dem use the ribbon ties, e hard to call am hanbok. B: I agree say dem gats respect the basic structure. But if we insist on the old style for material, length and how to fasten am too, fit be say nobody go wear am again. C: You mean say if nobody wear am, the tradition go cut off. B: Yes. Clothes wey dem keep for museum and clothes people wear dey preserved in different ways. I think the second one dey last longer.
texts.g:8a212118: A: Households wey dey live with their parents don reduce. E mean say people no value filial piety again? B: I no think say e reduce that much; e just change how people show am. Even when dem no live together, dem still show care by sharing hospital bills and keeping regular contact. C: That explanation assume say family still dey responsible for care. No be that assumption the problem? B: Your question make sense. But until the system give enough support, we no fit remove that assumption overnight. Na only after the system dey place we fit talk about filial piety as choice instead of obligation.
texts.g:7a77c58f: A: The number of households wey dey make kimchi by themselves dey fall. The kimchi-making culture dey disappear? B: Hard to judge am only by how many households make am. Even if people buy am, as long as dem still share with neighbours and check on dem, the culture dey continue. C: But if the practice of gathering to work together disappear, that sharing no go stop soon too? B: That concern make sense. Na why our institute dey put effort into recording and supporting the practice of gathering and sharing, instead of the taste of kimchi.
texts.g:bc4d2c30: A: Foreigners dey find am strange say dem delay work start times and even adjust plane takeoffs and landings on exam day. B: I understand am as one social promise to protect fairness for the exam. Na effort to make everybody take the test under the same conditions. C: But that kind of consideration no dey increase the pressure candidates feel? B: E fit. But if we withdraw the consideration, conditions go become unequal. I think say to reduce the pressure, we need to start by fixing the setup wey give people only one chance to take the exam, instead of changing how much consideration we show.
texts.g:8889d001: A: For some places, dem create system where people exchange work with each oda, counting by hours. Dem fit call am modern version of pumasi? B: I think e carry di same spirit. People pay back effort with relationships, no be money. C: But as e grow bigger, recording and managing hours no go cost more and make e less efficient? B: Dat na fair point. So I think system like dis work best for small village where people know each oda; e no make sense to spread am to whole city. But I want add say di value of dis system dey in relationships, no be efficiency.

texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:connector: Bound nouns and endings like -(으)ㄴ 만큼 show reason or degree, and dem common for formal reasoning in reports.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:concession: Markers for contrast or condition like “although”, “if”, and “however much” need matching endings later in di sentence.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:nominalise: Written reports turn clauses into noun phrases with -ㅁ/-기 endings, then attach object, subject, or agent particles.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:academicHedge: Academic writing make claims softer with set phrases like “could”, “may”, and “e hard to say for sure”, instead of saying dem certain.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:academicConn: Formal written arguments use set connecting and contrast phrases. Their endings must match di clauses wey dem connect.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:causeLink: Connectors like 이에 따라 and 결과적으로 connect a result to di cause just mentioned. So di clause before am must give di cause.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:hedge: Careful endings like -(으)ㄹ 것으로 보이다 and -기 어렵다 make a formal written claim sound uncertain instead of saying am for sure.
texts.n:k.k10.logic_debate:nominal: Noun phrases wey turn clauses into nouns, ending with -(으)ㄴ/는 + noun, -다는/-리라는 + noun, or -에 대한 + noun, shorten a whole clause so e fit work as subject of a formal sentence.

texts.n:k.k10.media_article:plainStyle: News and editorials use plain written style instead of polite spoken style, and dem use fixed reporting patterns.
texts.n:k.k10.media_article:reporting: Reporting verbs like “announced”, “pointed out”, or “revealed” join to reported clause with quotation ending.
texts.n:k.k10.media_article:forecast: Journalists express expectations with fixed endings meaning “is expected”, “seems likely”, or “is forecast”.
texts.n:k.k10.media_article:nominalise: Written reports turn clauses into noun phrases using -ㅁ/-기 endings, then add object, subject, or agent particles.
texts.n:k.k10.media_article:academicHedge: Academic writing soften claims with patterns like “could”, “may”, or “hard to say for sure”, instead of stating certainty.
texts.n:k.k10.media_article:academicConn: Formal written arguments use fixed connecting and contrast expressions; their endings must fit di clauses dem join.

texts.g:f804296d: Newspaper headline say “Effect of youth startup grants proven”. But article body say grant recipients one-year survival rate only 2 percentage points higher than comparison group, and researchers also say sample small and hard to apply broadly. For dis way, headline make stronger claim than di careful conclusion inside di article.
texts.g:593213fa: News headlines dey use question form more often now. Some people defend am say e show care because headline no claim unconfirmed facts. But headline like “Subsidy: e go work?” fit leave readers with only negative feeling even if article no answer di question. E quietly put claim inside by dressing am like question. Readers often only skim headline, so dem no get chance to correct di impression. Question-form headline make sense only if article give reasons for asking dat question.
texts.g:0e25e2a6: As race to break news fast dey intensify, unconfirmed information often enter headlines. Readers want news quickly, so speed itself no be problem. But even if dem correct mistake later, first headline impression hard to remove because correction articles no get as many readers as original. Speed and accuracy dey clash sometimes, but dat no mean say dem suppose solve am by shortening fact-checking. Even if e late, printing only confirmed facts na how to keep trust.
texts.g:53030fa1: Headline “Bicycle accidents double” grab readers attention immediately. E fair to say putting change rate first na efficient way to shorten information. But if starting number small, “double” no mean much, because same headline fit describe one case becoming two. But if hundreds of cases double, same headline carry very different weight. When headline use change rate, article must also show starting number so readers fit judge scale.
texts.g:bc267d69: Putting quotation marks for headline and repeating statement word for word fit look like objective reporting without reporter opinion. This method really useful to share statement accurately. But if dem pick only most shocking word from long statement and put am in headline, quotation become selection instead of full report. Quotation marks no guarantee accuracy; dem fit show how editor choose words. Readers suppose check article to see how quoted words were removed from context.
texts.g:63ea35cf: News articles dey use inverted pyramid structure, where dem put main point for first paragraph. E efficient because readers fit understand main idea even if dem stop after reading di beginning. But di more complex di matter, di more putting only conclusion in first paragraph push conditions and counterarguments to di back. So readers wey only read di beginning fit oversimplify di facts. Di weakness of dis structure na say plenty readers no read to di end. E better to summarize in first paragraph and also include di one most important condition.
texts.g:31402c52: Reader wey see headline “Consumer prices slow” fit easily think say prices don fall. People wey read economic news often know say dis short expression mean di rise in prices don slow down. But no be every reader get dis background, and if article only emphasize “slowing” while prices still high, e fit spread optimism wey no match wetin people dey feel. When you shorten technical terms, first think about whether readers get di same background knowledge.
texts.g:87c0595a: News headlines often use di word “controversy”. We suppose admit say na convenient short word to report matter wey people disagree about. But in practice, people attach “controversy” even to criticism from only a few people or suspicion with weak evidence, making e look like whole society dey divided. One word fit make di issue look bigger than e be. Before you use di expression, di main text suppose clearly show who dey argue about wetin.

texts.g:0c1b4b47: One newspaper report with headline 'Unemployment jump, sign of crisis' say this month's unemployment rate increase by 0.3 percentage points from last month to 3.4 percent. But the Employment Trends Institute announcement say the survey use sample households and get statistical error of plus or minus 0.4 percentage points. When a change dey within the margin of error, e hard to know if na real change or just chance from the sampling. So even if the article body show the exact numbers, the headline word 'jump' stronger than wetin the figures fit support. E safer to check the trend across several months before judging, instead of focusing on one month's change.
texts.g:b5385d29: For an opinion poll on a new-town development plan, 48 percent support am and 45 percent oppose am, and one broadcaster report say 'Support for development dey ahead.' The sampling error for this poll na plus or minus 3.1 percentage points at 95 percent confidence level. Since the three-point difference between support and opposition dey within the margin of error, statistically we no fit say which side bigger. For this kind case, writing 'opinion dey split evenly' match the data better. If a report turn the number difference straight into a ranking, readers fit understand am like a settled fact.
texts.g:408798cc: One local newspaper use the headline 'Bicycle accidents for the district double.' The article body show say accidents increase from 3 last year to 6 this year. By percentage alone, na 100 percent increase, but because the actual number small, even a chance difference of one or two cases fit change the percentage plenty. On the other hand, car accidents for the same area increase by 5 percent, from 1,200 to 1,260, but dem no put am for headline. Which of these risks readers really need to know? We no suppose read the percentage wey the headline emphasize as direct sign of how important the article be.
texts.g:f1021423: For bar chart in one article, dem draw average rent for Region A more than twice high as Region B. But vertical axis start from 800,000 won, no be 0. Actual figures na 920,000 won for A and 850,000 won for B, difference just above 8 percent. If dem cut off starting point, even small difference fit look like big gap. Even if graph shape seem to support article claim, visual impression go fool readers unless dem check scale and units.
texts.g:9369abc2: For weather articles, phrase “highest temperature since records began” need careful interpretation. For example, Onsaemi observatory record temperatures since 1998, so “since records began” only mean highest in record of about 20 years. You no fit compare am directly with record from other places wey don observe for almost 100 years. Plus, if area around observatory don become city and heat dey collect more easily, temperature rise fit come from changes in local environment too, no be only climate change. So phrase fit be true, but e no directly mean say na proof of climate change.
texts.g:f28ddb3b: One article headline say “Food additive A raises cancer risk.” But researcher wey dem quote for article only talk say, “In tests with mice, tumors increase in some cases with high doses, so we no fit rule out possibility of risk to people too.” Dis statement mean say dem never rule out risk, no be say risk don prove. Headline remove condition “possibility” and limitation “mouse experiment”, and leave only conclusion. Quoting person no mean say the caution in their words reach readers too.
texts.g:8f4d8e8f: Readers wey see article titled “Average salary of office workers: 52 million won” worry say their own income below average. But table from same survey show median as 41 million won. Di fact say average pass median by more than 10 million won mean say small number of high earners pull average up. For data wey skew to one side, like income, average fit no represent ordinary people situation. Number in headline no wrong, but readers worry mostly because dem choose dat measure.

texts.g:4e66256a: Two big delivery platforms dey compete by cutting fees and advertising benefits for shop owners. texts.g:392498f6: People wey criticize specialization call a researcher wey focus deeply on one field a 'frog in a well.' But water only dey spring up when the well deep. texts.g:a8777528: People dey commonly believe say when one joint research project get plenty people wey dey in charge, wahala go happen. texts.g:1f6577ed: People dey point out say most members of review committee na people wey don work for long time for the industry wey dem dey review. texts.g:0a684b7e: People often quote di proverb say habits wey person learn for childhood dey last all life to support early education. texts.g:8342bfa1: “Carbon neutrality” mean make di amount of greenhouse gas wey people release equal di amount dem absorb or remove, so net emission reach zero. E no mean say dem must remove all emissions completely; e mean balance di parts wey hard to reduce with forest planting or capture technology. So to achieve carbon neutrality, dem need both to reduce emissions and find ways to offset dem.
texts.g:b726ec3e: A: People no agree whether benchmark rate suppose reduce. Make we first hear from Dr. B. B: If dem reduce rates, interest pressure go fall and spending fit recover. But household debt high now, so extra money likely go pay debt instead of spending. C: I understand di worry, but we no fit just watch economy sink, abi? B: I no dey against rate cut itself. I mean if dem reduce rates without steps to manage debt, expected benefit fit cut to half.
texts.g:fbb5abf4: A: People disagree about law to add CCTV for alleys. B: Some studies say e help prevent crime, but risk say people go use footage beyond its purpose also high. So I think law must clearly state reason for installation and how long to keep recordings. C: I think problem na to increase surveillance devices wey never prove say dem work. B: You correct say evidence still no enough. But e hard to agree say dem must stop installation completely. We fit use dem for set period, check results, and add rule to remove dem if dem no work.
texts.g:b74e7fde: A: Some people say make we delay climate steps because climate model predictions fit get errors. C: If models give different numbers, e no make sense to wait for more certainty before we start costly policies? B: True, models dey differ. But difference na about how much temperature go rise, no be whether e go rise at all. Also, damage for worst case far bigger than cost of preparation. C: So you mean uncertainty alone no be reason to delay? B: For delay to make sense, uncertainty must even change which direction things dey go. Dat no be di case now.
texts.g:8ac184e0: A: We dey discuss whether to give youth support payment to all young people or only those wey get low income. B: If dem divide people by income, recipients fit feel shame, and young people just above the cutoff no go get support. I support payment for everybody. C: The problem na funding. To give everybody, you must either cut the amount plenty or raise tax. B: I no fit deny that. Na why I no dey argue make dem start full program straight away. I dey think make dem begin with one smaller age group, then widen am after dem see the effect.
texts.g:c517e875: A: The district office wan reduce service counters and move to online applications. C: Online service reduce cost and wait time. Counter staff dey limited. B: E clear say efficiency go improve. But for residents wey no sabi online services well, the counter na their only way to get service. When one channel disappear, the first people wey suffer inconvenience usually be those wey already find am hard to make their voice heard. C: Still, the staffing problem no solve. B: So I no dey propose to close the counters; make dem reduce service during hours wey few people use am, and move those staff to a help desk.
texts.g:9e6048cb: A: People don debate for long whether literal or free translation better for classical poetry. B: I think say literal translation suppose be the starting point. With free translation, there be risk say translator interpretation go reach reader as if na the original. C: But no be interpretation already to choose one meaning and move each word across? Translation without interpretation no dey. B: Na true. Person no fit escape interpretation. Wetin I mean no be to remove interpretation, na to help readers notice where the translator add interpretation. Notes fit do that work.
texts.g:e5b59eb3: A: Di issue be whether workers for delivery platforms suppose count as employees. C: These people choose flexible work time, and if dem call dem employees, dem go lose dat flexibility. B: I agree say flexibility get value. But if platform algorithm dey control which work they get, e nearly the same as person dey direct them. Still, I no say make every case count as employment; I think dem suppose check how much control each case get. C: So how you propose make dem handle protection like work accident insurance? B: Apart from deciding whether person be employee, dem fit first put basic safety support against accidents in place.

texts.n:k.k10.sino_four:fourChar: Four-character idioms come from Chinese characters. Each syllable carry one meaning, and people use di full phrase like noun or adjective.
texts.n:k.k10.sino_four:ctx: Understand a four-character idiom from di clause around am. Words for cause and result before it show if situation lucky, unlucky, too much, or praise-worthy.

texts.g:966842b0: Recently, more people dey lose plenty money after dem believe sweet talk wey promise 'your capital safe and 20% profit every month.' For normal investment, the higher the profit, the higher the risk. Na for that reason make person doubt promise of big profit with zero risk. Instead make sweet words carry us go rush, we need habit to first check whether official body register the company.
texts.g:36da0494: One food company hide product problem wey e know about, but one worker wey report the matter from inside finally bring everything to light. Plenty people feel relief and talk say justice always win. But say the final result correct the matter no mean say the process too follow correct way. Some consumers don already get hurt, and if the monitoring system weak, the truth fit remain buried. Justice no dey win by itself; e fit happen only when institutions and courage support am.
texts.g:acf2b5ae: The saying say more na better fit work for things, but e hard to apply am to information. When material plenty, e fit look like say grounds for judgment don increase, but really, the time and effort to separate the useful ones don increase too. Plus, when material wey origin no clear join inside, e fit make the conclusion even less clear. Wetin matter no be how much you gather, na how correct you choose and use reliable material.
texts.g:099e31d2: People wey lose their jobs during recession often hear 'Saeongjima' as comfort. E mean say person no fit predict the good and bad things wey life bring, so good days go come if you wait. The old man for the story no rush judge whether the luck good or bad, whether im horse run comot or e come back. But this phrase no mean make person siddon idle and wait for good luck. Comfort words no fit take the place of practical support. People wey no get work need to calmly accept uncertainty, and dem also need real support like new skills training and protection for their income.
texts.g:52aa979d: When one company propose changing the pay plan so the total yearly salary stay the same, but base pay go down and performance bonus share go up, the union object and call am 'Josammosa.' The monkeys for the story foolish because dem miss say whether na three for morning or four, na still seven for the day. But this plan get one thing wey no dey inside the monkey story. Bonus fit reduce depending on company results, and base pay na the measure for severance pay and loan checks. Even if the total look the same, if na different people dey carry the risk, hard to say say na Josammosa matter.
texts.g:cdec0eb0: One local festival do well to attract tourists, and visitors increase every year. But events wey residents join reduce, and the stage begin focus on performers from outside. People criticize this change as 'reversal of host and guest.' The residents wey maintain the tradition suppose be the festival hosts, but now the visitors' taste dey decide the event content. Still, no blame the increase in visitors itself. The problem na say, to welcome visitors, the host don get push out from im own place. Make dem judge festival success not by number of visitors, but by whether residents still dey the center of the stage.
texts.g:17a6db45: Plenty people use 'Daegi-manseong' to argue against choosing gifted children early. Dem talk say some talents bloom late, so people no suppose sort children early. But this answer get one gap too. Since Daegi-manseong dey talk about a great vessel wey finish late, e no tell us about the countless cases wey people wait for late blooming but e never happen. To discuss when selection suppose happen by collecting only success stories no enough evidence. Instead, make dem check whether selection end after one round or whether people get another chance later.
texts.g:ef984356: Anytime people talk say dem wan cut budget for disaster response drill, dem bring the saying 'Yubi-muhwan' as argument to answer dem. This saying no wrong, but e no strong to convince people. When preparation work well, nothing happen, so the success no show as visible event. The fact say accident no happen fit mean say the drills work, or fit mean say drills no need from beginning. So to convince people wey control budget, wetin dem need no be slogan but data wey estimate the damage wey for happen if no drills dey.
texts.g:7d9c642e: One manufacturer run big advert to promote eco-friendly management, but the company disclosure documents say greenhouse gas emissions actually rise for the same period. E easy to call am 'Pyori-budong.' But Pyori-budong mean say outside and inside no match, and to talk so you gats know the inside. If the advert explain plan to reduce emissions and the plan still dey implementation stage, the gap wit current figures fit be time delay instead of deceit. Make dem judge after dem confirm how specific the reduction plan be and whether dem dey carry am out as promised.
texts.g:5b588c16: One team wey don work together for long dey understand each other without talking. People call am 'Isim-jeonsim' and see am as ideal teamwork. But this way get cost. Standards wey everybody understand without talk no dey written down, so dem fit disappear all at once when members change. Also, the belief say 'we understand without talking' fit remove the chance to show say each person understand things differently. Isim-jeonsim strong only when important standards don already enter writing.
